title: 05.12.26 Public Hearing - Chipman/Stake Center Annexation
agenda_text:
Public Hearing Notice - Chipman/Stake Center Annexation
Notice is hereby given that a petition for annexation was filed with American Fork City. The petition, which was accepted by the city council on October 22, 2024, covers approximately 24 acres consisting of property located at approximately 515 South 100 West.  The city recorder certified the petition, and the legislative body provided notice according to Utah Code 10-2-406. A 30-day period was allowed to give property owners and affected entities the opportunity to submit written protests. A public hearing was previously held on February 25, 2025.
A public hearing will be held on Tuesday, May 12, at 7 p.m. at the American Fork City Hall (31 N. Church Street) to allow the public to comment on the Chipman/Stake Center Annexation. After the public hearing, American Fork City may choose to deny or grant the petition and annex the area described in the petition. 
The complete annexation petition is available for inspection and copying at the American Fork City Recorder's office (51 E. Main Street, American Fork) or by emailing tlurker@americanfork.gov
Dated this 30th day of April 2026.
/s/ Terilyn Lurker, City Recorder

Amending Section 17.9, the Code Text Amendment clarifies improvements, public or private, required to be included in the performance guarantee that applicants provide to the City and clarifies expiration requirements.  

 	Description: The Code Text Amendment clarifies that performance guarantees need to be in place for the duration of the project without an expiration or that if they do have an expiration, a renewal will be required to ensure that a performance guarantee is in place until the project is completed and City Council has accepted the infrastructure and released the performance guarantee. It also requires the improvement warranty to be in place until the durability period for the project is completed, the applicant has completed all punch list items, and all public infrastructure has been inspected by City Staff and meets all City standards. If the improvement warranty has an expiration, a renewal shall be required until the above-mentioned items are complete. Further, it quantifies the contingency amount required for performance guarantees. Private infrastructure that is required to meet various qualifying criteria as outlined in Utah State code shall be included in the performance guarantee.

title: ERDA City Council Member Vacancy Notice
agenda_text:
Erda City 2026 City Council Vacancy Public Notice

City Council member Sheldon Birch has resigned from his Erda City Council Office effective December 31, 2026. This notice is to inform the public of the vacancy in District 5 and the procedure for filling that vacancy. The vacancy is filled by a vote from the remaining Erda City Council Members and Sheldon Birch who has reserved his right to participate in the vote under Utah Code 20A-1-510(4)(a). The applicants who must live in District 5 will be interviewed in an open public meeting and the vote to fill the vacancy will be done at that same meeting.
The public meeting where the vacancy will be filled will be  
Date- Thursday, December 10, 2026 
Time- 6:00 pm 
Place- 2163 West Erda Way, Erda, UT, 84074 (Erda City Office/Fire Station) 
If someone is interested in applying for the vacancy they must contact and meet with the City Recorder, Jennifer Poole, and file an application (in person). 
Jennifer Poole 
435-243-5577 
jpoole@erda.gov  
In person appointments need to be made before the deadline.  
Application Submission Deadline Friday December 4, 2026 5:00 pm (this is a hard deadline, no exceptions) 
Available Appointment Dates Times 9:00 am- 5:00 pm Nov 19-20, 2026 Nov 23-25, 2026 Nov 30, - Dec 4, 2026 Applications will be available to the public as they are submitted and uploaded, please visit  Erda Vacancy Filings 2026  The Procedure for filling a midterm vacancy in municipality office are found in Utah State Code 20A-1-510

PUBLIC OPEN HOUSE
PROPOSED DATA CENTER REGULATIONS
Possible Quorum of Planning Commission Present

PUBLIC NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that an open house regarding proposed regulations for Data Centers within Grantsville City will be held on Wednesday, September 30, 2026, from 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. at the Grantsville City Police Station, 50 Bowery Street, Grantsville, Utah.
The open house is intended to provide an opportunity for residents to learn about the proposed Data Center regulations, ask questions, discuss the proposed regulations with City staff, and provide feedback.
The open house is not a meeting of the Grantsville City Planning Commission or Grantsville City Council and will not be conducted or led by the Planning Commission and/or City Council. Members of the Planning Commission and/or City Council may attend the open house, and a quorum of the Planning Commission and/or City Council may be present. No formal Planning Commission or City Council meeting will be convened, and no action or decisions will be taken by the Planning Commission or City Council during the open house.
The proposed Data Center regulations are anticipated to be presented to the Grantsville City Planning Commission on October 20, 2026, at which time the Planning Commission may discuss the proposed regulations and make a recommendation in accordance with the posted Planning Commission agenda.

Bill Cobabe
Grantsville Community Development Director

Posted on September 22, 2026, in accordance with the 
Utah Open and Public Meetings Act.

NOTICE OF ORDINANCE ADOPTION

PUBLIC NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the Grantsville City Council adopted the following ordinances at its regular City Council meetings held on the dates identified below:

- Ordinance 2026-05, adopted August 19, 2026, approves the rezoning of property located at approximately 500 West Apple Street for the Apple Street Townhomes
Subdivision to RM-15 (Multiple Residential District), excluding approximately 1.19 acres retained for commercial use along the SR-138 frontage.

- Ordinance 2026-29, adopted September 16, 2026, amends Chapter 15 of the Grantsville Land Use and Management Code to allow Micro-Entrepreneurship as a conditional use in the R-1-8, R-1-12, R-1-21, RM-7, and RM-15 zoning districts, subject to existing standards, operating limitations, and separate application and approval requirements.

- Ordinance 2026-30, adopted September 16, 2026, amends Chapters 2, 6, and 7 of the Grantsville Land Use Ordinance to remove the minimum 100-foot frontage requirement for home occupation permit eligibility, remove the fixed 60-foot driveway separation requirement near intersections, and clarify referral of conditional use applications to the Planning Commission when public comments raise concerns.

- Ordinance 2026-28, adopted October 5, 2026, amends Chapter 9 of the Grantsville Land Use Ordinance to update landscaping, waterwise landscaping, turf, irrigation, park strip, parkway, and median standards, including requirements for landscape plans, installation, maintenance, and approved plant materials.

Complete copies of the adopted ordinances are available for review at the Grantsville City Recorder's office during regular business hours and online through the City's website at https://grantsville.municipalcodeonline.com/book?type=orddoc#name=2026 and the Utah Public Notice Website at https://www.utah.gov/pmn/sitemap/publicbody/1840.html.

GRANTSVILLE CITY
NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING
PROPOSED FISCAL YEAR 2027 BUDGET AMENDMENTS

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the Grantsville City Council will hold a public hearing on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, at 7:00 p.m., or as soon thereafter as the matter may be heard, at the Council Chambers of Grantsville City Hall, located at 429 E. Main Street, Grantsville, Utah and electronically via Zoom, to receive public comment regarding proposed amendments to the City's Fiscal Year 2027 budget, covering July 1, 2026, through June 30, 2027.

The public hearing will be conducted pursuant to Utah Code Sections 10-6-127, 10-6-113, and 10-6-114.

The proposed amendments include increased appropriations for general government professional services, dues and fees; library employee appreciation and grant expenditures; rodeo expenses; Building Department computer software; Community Development grant expenses; and Planning Commission stipends. The amendments also include reductions to Parks and Recreation and Cemetery salary appropriations, increases to Water and Sewer salary appropriations, a corresponding reduction to the Water capital water line project appropriation, and a reduction to the Sewer contribution to fund balance.

The proposed budget increases the amount budgeted for use of General Fund balance from $1,593,698 to $1,665,104, an increase of $71,406. The total Water and Sewer fund budgets remain unchanged, with adjustments to appropriations within those funds.

Copies of the proposed budget amendments will be available for public inspection before the hearing at Grantsville City Hall, located at 429 E. Main Street, Grantsville, Utah and on the City's website at www.grantsvilleut.gov.

All interested persons are invited to attend the public hearing and will be given an opportunity to speak for or against the proposed amendments, including any affected revenue or expenditure item. Written comments may also be submitted to the City Recorder at afairbourne@gran

COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG)
FIRST PUBLIC HEARING NOTICE

Notice is hereby given that Grantsville City will hold a public hearing on December 2, 2026 at Grantsville City Hall, located at 429 E Main St., Grantsville Utah, as well as electronically via Zoom at 6:45 p.m. Grantsville City is eligible to apply for funding under the Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Small Cities Program, a federally funded program administered by the State of Utah, Division of Housing and Community Development (HCD).

Grantsville City is eligible to apply for CDBG funding provided Grantsville City meets the applicable program requirements.

The purpose of the public hearing is to provide citizens with pertinent information about the
Community Development Block Grant program and to allow for discussion of possible projects. This public hearing will cover eligible activities, program requirements, and expected funding allocations in the region. The CDBG Program can fund a broad range of activities, including, but not limited to: construction of public works and facilities, e.g., water and sewer lines, fire stations, acquisition of real property, and provision of public services such as food banks or homeless shelters. In the event that Grantsville City chooses to apply for CDBG funding, a second public hearing will be held at a later time to discuss the project. Further information can be obtained by contacting Alexis Stewart at 435-884-4600 or by email at astewart@grantsvilleut.gov.  

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, individuals needing special accommodations (including auxiliary communicative aids and services) during this hearing should notify Alicia Fairbourne at 435-884-4603 or by email at afairbourne@grantsvilleut.gov at 429 E Main St., Grantsville, Utah, 84029 at least three days prior to the hearing.
